description: Seeing Earth whole, understanding it deeply.
summary:
EARTHPULSE-X is an interactive Earth-system analysis platform for Uttarakhand, India, built for NASA Space Apps’ “Be an Earth System Trend Detective” challenge. It brings together ten years of NASA satellite observations—land-surface temperature and vegetation greenness from MODIS, morning and evening soil moisture from SMAP, and precipitation from GPM—into a quality-filtered monthly record across Uttarakhand’s 13 districts.

The dashboard helps users investigate what is changing, when and where changes occur, how large they are, and how reliable the evidence is. It combines maps and time series with autocorrelation-adjusted trend tests, Sen’s slope, multiple-testing correction, seasonal anomaly detection, sensor comparisons, uncertainty analysis, and exploratory forecasts.

The project matters because Himalayan communities face interacting environmental pressures, yet satellite signals can be incomplete or difficult to interpret. EARTHPULSE-X makes these patterns and data limitations easier to explore, supporting research and awareness. Its anomaly and forecast outputs are investigative signals, not official warnings or proof of causes.
details:
EARTHPULSE-X helps people investigate how Uttarakhand’s environment is changing—and see how reliable the evidence is. We built an interactive platform using a decade of NASA satellite observations: MODIS land-surface temperature and vegetation greenness, SMAP morning and evening soil moisture, and GPM precipitation. It harmonizes these different measurements into a monthly record and lets users explore regional and district patterns through maps, timelines, and comparisons.

The platform addresses the challenge’s central questions: What is changing, when and where is it changing, how much, and how strong is the evidence? Its analyses include autocorrelation-adjusted trend tests, Sen’s slope, multiple-testing correction, seasonal anomaly detection, cross-sensor relationships, data-quality comparisons, uncertainty analysis, and exploratory forecasts. A multi-hazard view helps users investigate combinations of signals associated with drought, floods, heat, and vegetation stress. These are research indicators, not official alerts or confirmed impacts.

Our creative contribution is UG-ESI—Uncertainty-Guided Earth System Intelligence: we bring trend detection, data coverage, uncertainty, and signal interactions into one workflow, so users can see both the pattern and its limitations. We considered Uttarakhand’s varied terrain, seasonality, different sensor resolutions and schedules, missing observations, autocorrelation, and the risk of mistaking correlation for cause.

We developed the project with Python, Streamlit, JavaScript, HTML/CSS, and libraries including Pandas, NumPy, GeoPandas, xarray, and Plotly. AI services support explanations grounded in the project’s computed results. The platform runs as software and needs no specialized hardware. Our aim is to make satellite evidence easier to understand and support better-informed research and environmental awareness.
